skill.displayName: AI Short Film Finalization — Route C (Flow Free)

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed AI film workflow, but it asks to automate a logged-in Chrome profile and generates executable shell commands from editable project data, creating review-worthy security risk.

dimensions.detail: The macOS startup command force-kills all Google Chrome processes and relaunches the default profile with remote debugging enabled, which is disproportionate and can expose unrelated authenticated browser activity.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup installs npm and pip dependencies without exact pins, lockfiles, hashes, or registry constraints, and uses fixed local WorkBuddy paths rather than a reproducible least-privilege install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly reuse the user's existing Google login through Chrome CDP on port 9222 and later tell the AI/operator to execute exported remediation commands, giving the workflow broad browser-session and shell influence beyond a narrowly scoped media-processing tool.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor or service persistence was found, but dependencies are installed into reusable environments and the remote-debugging browser profile can remain available until manually closed, increasing residual privilege exposure.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated AI short-film finalization purpose is mostly coherent with the artifacts, but the package describes a broad end-to-end generator while only shipping the review-console generator and template; users may expect capabilities and safety boundaries that are not fully present in the package.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in an isolated project and browser profile, not your everyday Chrome profile. Do not run exported execution_cmd values blindly; inspect or convert them to structured arguments first. Pin dependencies before use, avoid the pkill Chrome startup command, and treat storyboard/project-name input as untrusted until the HTML and shell escaping issues are fixed.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted: the skill description promises full generation, composition, narration, trailer, and review capabilities, but the shipped executable artifact only creates a review package from existing media; this is a disclosure and coherence issue, not evidence of malicious intent.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted: the skill asks for shell, file, browser automation, package install, and authenticated web access without explicit least-privilege scoping or containment.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as purpose-aligned but concerning: reusing an already logged-in Chrome profile is disclosed and helps automate Google Flow, but CDP grants broad control over the selected browser profile and cookies.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: force-killing Google Chrome is not necessary for the core film workflow and may destroy unrelated browser state.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted with concern: command generation is explicitly part of the review loop, but the exported execution_cmd values are high-impact because they are intended to be executed later.
[AST4] expected: Downgraded: subprocess use in review-final-v4.py invokes ffmpeg/ffprobe with argument arrays and shell=False for expected media extraction; this is not direct shell injection by itself.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded for security verdict: the hard-coded Chinese UI and English prompt recommendation are usability and disclosure limitations, not a material local-security concern here.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: review-final-v4.py inserts raw manifest JSON and project name into an executable HTML script context, so storyboard or path values containing script-closing markup could execute JavaScript in the generated review page.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: review-director-template.html builds shell command strings from shot titles, prompts, narration, and subtitle text with insufficient escaping, and the skill instructs downstream execution of those commands.
[T05] expected: Accepted as purpose-aligned but overbroad: Chrome CDP with the default logged-in profile exposes more authority than needed for a single Google Flow task.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted: runtime dependency installation is unpinned and integrity is not verified, making the effective installed code change over time.
